'''Nina Irene McClelland''' (21 August 1929 &ndash; 16 August 2020) was an American chemist. She was dean emeritus and professor of chemistry at the [[University of Toledo]].

==Early life and education==
McClelland was raised by her mother Lillian McClelland, who worked as a foreign language teacher.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lillian McClelland |url=http://www.bedfordyes.com/images/BhsMcLelland.pdf |website=bedfordyes.com |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=October 25, 1997}}</ref> Growing up, McClelland took vocal lessons and was taught six languages by her mother.<ref name = "x">{{cite web |title=UT News |url=https://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/UTnews2008/2008.09.02.UTnews.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |page=1 |date=September 2, 2008}}</ref> McClelland's aunt, [[Fern Mervos]], was a professor in the department of mathematics at the University of Toledo.<ref>{{cite web |title=UT NEWS |url=https://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/UTnews2008/2008.02.25.UTnews.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |page=4 |date=February 25, 2008}}</ref> McClelland says she was very close to her aunt and as a child would visit her at work.<ref name = "x"/>

McClelland graduated from [[Gibsonburg High School]] and pursued a degree in mathematics at the [[University of Toledo]]. She eventually earned her [[Bachelor of Science]] and [[Master of Science]] from the University of Toledo before graduating with a doctoral degree in environmental chemistry from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1968.<ref name = ":1">{{cite news |last1=Henry |first1=Tom |title=UT dedicating new lab in honor of one of its most distinguished scientists |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/local/environment/2019/09/18/university-of-toledo-dedicating-new-lab-in-honor-of-one-of-its-most-distinguished-scientists-on-thursday/stories/20190918126 |access-date=October 3, 2019 |publisher=The Blade |date=September 18, 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1967, while earning her PhD, McClelland became involved with the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FROM THE CHAIR OF THE BOARD, NINA I. McCLELLAND |url=http://pubsapp.acs.org/cen/125th/html/7913nina.html? |website=pubsapp.acs.org |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=March 26, 2001}}</ref> The next year, McClelland was named president and chief executive officer of the National Sanitation Foundation International.<ref name = "y">{{cite web |last1=Hayes |first1=Krista M. |title=UT alumna to receive American National Standards Institute medal |url=https://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/UTnews2006-04/2005.10.03.UTnews.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |page=2 |date=October 3, 2005}}</ref> During her time at the National Sanitation Foundation, McClelland led the International Clean Water program and served on the National Academy of Sciences Committee on Water Treatment Chemicals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rowland |first1=Kyle |title=Wildlife Federation recognizes UT alumna |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/local/2016/04/01/Wildlife-Federation-recognizes-UT-alumna.html |access-date=October 3, 2019 |publisher=The Blad |date=April 1, 2016}}</ref> She also created a Water Quality Index to report water quality in lakes, rivers and streams. After the [[Safe Drinking Water Act]] was passed in the 1970s, McClelland also helped create the governmental standard for chemicals to treat drinking water.<ref name = "Gold T">{{cite web |title=Alumni to be honored at annual Homecoming Gala |url=http://news.utoledo.edu/index.php/category/colleges/colleges-jhcoehshs |website=news.utoledo.edu|access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=October 22, 2014}}</ref> In 1986, McClelland sat on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Advisory Committee.<ref>{{cite book |title=U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Advisory Committees, Charters, Rosters, and Accomplishments |date=April 14, 2017 |publisher=U.S. Environmental Protection Agency |page=31 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tc6piMai7OsC&q=nina+McClelland+professor+at+University+of+Michigan&pg=PA31}}</ref>

In 1991, McClelland was the recipient of the Walter S. Mangold Award from the [[National Environmental Health Association]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Listing of Past Walter S. Mangold Award Winners |url=https://www.neha.org/walter-s-mangold-award-winners |website=neha.org |access-date=October 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828023446/https://www.neha.org/walter-s-mangold-award-winners |archive-date=August 28, 2017}}</ref> In 1993, McClelland spoke in front of the United States Congress Committee on Environment and Public Works to promote cost-effective treatments to assist smaller, isolated communities in accessing clean drinking water.<ref>{{cite book |title=Safe Drinking Water Act Amendments of 1993 |date=1994 |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |isbn=9780160439209 |pages=154–155 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lvxcTZpgxEkC&q=nina+McClelland++International+Clean+Water+program&pg=PA154 |access-date=October 3, 2019}}</ref> In 1995, McClelland was awarded chairwoman emeritus status<ref>{{cite news |title=Nina McClelland, 67 |url=https://www.crainsdetroit.com/article/19970331/SUB/160609727/nina-mcclelland-67 |access-date=October 3, 2019 |publisher=Crain's Detroit Business |date=March 31, 1997}}</ref> and started her own, independent consulting firm.<ref name = "fellow">{{cite web |last1=Strunk |first1=Jon |title=Dean emerita honored by American Chemical Society |url=http://news.utoledo.edu/index.php/09_28_2011/mcclelland-honored-as-american-chemical-society-fellow |website=news.utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=September 28, 2011}}</ref> As well, McClelland was later elected American Chemical Society Board of Directors Chair.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Morrisey |first1=Susan |title=Society Welcomes Its New Officers |url=http://pubsapp.acs.org/cen/topstory/8004/8004notw6.html? |website=pubsapp.acs.org |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=January 28, 2002}}</ref>

McClelland was appointed an adjunct professor of chemistry at the University of Toledo in 2003.<ref name = ":1"/> She was also the recipient of an honorary degree from the university.<ref>{{cite web |title=FEBRUARY 26, 2003 MINUTES PART TWO |url=http://www.utoledo.edu/offices/trustees/agendas_minutes/2003_agendas_minutes/02_26_2003_part_2.html |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019}}</ref> Two years later, she was honored with the Wham Leadership Medal from the American National Standards Institute.<ref name = "y"/> In 2008, McClelland was promoted to interim dean of the college of arts and sciences.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Klinger |first1=Tobin J. |title=Interim dean for College of Arts and Sciences named |url=https://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/UTnews2008/2008.08.18.UTnews.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=August 18, 2008}}</ref> Her duties included improving the college of arts and sciences strategic assessment.<ref>{{cite web |title=People on the Move |url=https://www.ansi.org/news_publications/news_story?menuid=7&articleid=4d975036-4022-4747-91d5-0804580af12e |website=ansi.org |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=August 15, 2008}}</ref> The interim honorific was dropped in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=YEAR IN REVIEW |url=http://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/2009.12.14.UTnews.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |page=6 |date=December 14, 2009 |quote=Dr. Nina McClelland, interim dean of the College of Arts and Sciences since August 2008, receives a contract extension through 2010-11 academic year and interim is dropped from her title}}</ref> She was also inducted into the [[Ohio Women's Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Governor announces 2010 Ohio Women's Hall of Fame inductees |url=https://abc7.com/archive/7589457/ |website=abc7.com |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=August 3, 2010}}</ref>  The following year, McClelland was named a Fellow of the  American Chemical Society<ref name = "fellow"/> and retired.<ref name = "fellow"/>

In 2014, McClelland was the recipient of the University's Gold T Award for her "outstanding career accomplishment."<ref name = "Gold T"/> Two years later, in 2016, McClelland was the recipient of the [[National Wildlife Federation]]'s Women in Conservation Award for her contributions to promoting clean energy and protecting clean water supplies.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gearheart |first1=Ashley |title=Alumna/dean emerita honored by National Wildlife Federation |url=https://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/2016.05.02.UTNews.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |page=6 |date=May 2, 2016}}</ref> She was also honored by the [[Sigma Xi]] Scientific Research Honor Society<ref>{{cite web |title=2017 ANNUAL BANQUET |url=http://umich.edu/~sigmaxi/Documents/Program_for_2017_Banquet.pdf |website=umich.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=April 19, 2017}}</ref> and granted a symbolic key to the city of Toledo.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=city_of_toledo|number=913026116662722561|date=September 27, 2017|title= speaking at OAWWA conference where she just gave #SafeDrinkingWater Pioneer, Dr. Nina McClelland, a key to the city.}}</ref> In April, McClelland was one of five women given the Dr. Alice H. Skeens Outstanding Woman Award.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kroll |first1=Vicki L. |title=University Women's Commission recognizes employees, awards scholarships to students |url=https://www.utoledo.edu/offices/marketing/utnews/pdfs/UTnewspdfs/April%2017.pdf |website=utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |page=8 |date=April 17, 2017}}</ref>

In 2019, McClelland was honored in front of the United States Congress for her accomplishments in preserving clean water.<ref>{{cite web |title=HONORING THE ACCOMPLISHMENTS OF DR. NINA McCLELLAND; Congressional Record Vol. 165, No. 151 |url=https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record/2019/09/19/extensions-of-remarks-section/article/E1178-2 |website=congress.gov |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=September 19, 2019}}</ref> The University of Toledo also dedicated a new Laboratory for Water Chemistry and Environmental Analysis in her name.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Christine |first1=Billau |title=New Chemistry Lab to be Dedicated in Honor of Water Quality Leader, UToledo alum Sept. 19 |url=http://news.utoledo.edu/index.php/09_17_2019/new-chemistry-lab-to-be-dedicated-in-honor-of-water-quality-leader-utoledo-alum-sept-19 |website=news.utoledo.edu |access-date=October 3, 2019 |date=September 17, 2019}}</ref>

She died on August 16, 2020, at the age of 90.<ref>[https://www.toledoblade.com/news/deaths/2020/08/17/nina-mcclelland-famous-ut-educated-scientist-dies-at-90/stories/20200817122 Nina McClelland, famous UT-educated scientist, dies at 90]</ref>
